result.title: Beyond Row-Level Prediction: Evaluating and Learning Composition for Reusable Table Representations
result.summary: Tables are compositional, with content spread across a schema, cell values, rows, and columns. Large-scale operations such as retrieval, overlap estimation, deduplication, and data curation need these local signals composed into one reusable embedding vector per table. Table representation methods, however, are mostly evaluated through row-level prediction or supervised downstream tasks, which do not measure table-level embedding quality directly. We introduce a benchmark that evaluates table-level embeddings through four desiderata: consistency under partial views, discriminability across label granularities, robustness to benign perturbations, and efficiency. Across twelve methods on synthetic and real corpora, lightweight schema- and text-based fingerprints are among the strongest. The sharpest contrast comes from two tabular foundation models, TabPFN and ConTextTab: although both are strong row-level predictors, their states, composed by mean, max, or three further parameter-free pooling rules, trail the strongest fingerprints. We therefore ask whether the gap lies in the encoder or in the compositional rule. Keeping ConTextTab frozen, we learn only the compositional rule over its cell states, using support-conditioned distribution matching (SCDM), a self-supervised loss we propose that matches the distribution of embedding similarities to the distribution of partition overlaps within and across tables. Across all fifteen head configurations, the learned rule raises the Spearman correlation between embedding similarity and partial-view overlap from 0.04 to 0.43-0.50 on synthetic data and improves triplet ranking, clustering, and retrieval, with smaller but systematic gains on real data. A downstream parent-table retrieval task confirms these findings. How local states are composed, and with what objective, substantially affects the quality of table-level embeddings.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出表格级嵌入的评测基准，以部分视图一致性、标签粒度可区分性、良性扰动鲁棒性与效率四项准则比较十二种方法，发现行级预测强的表格基座模型在均值/最大等池化规则下反而不如轻量指纹；随后冻结 ConTextTab，仅用自监督的支撑条件分布匹配（SCDM）学习 cell states 的组合规则。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心问题是「局部状态如何组合成单一表示、以及用什么目标监督组合」，与视觉 token 或推理状态聚合成 latent、池化规则设计与相似度分布层面的监督有可供核查的线索；但研究对象是表格而非视觉推理，迁移价值需进一步确认。
